word:hebrew:H1074.explanation: Bokeru is the personal name of an Israelite listed among Azel’s sons.

word:hebrew:H1096.explanation: Belteshazzar is a name used for Daniel.

word:hebrew:H110.explanation: Adbeel is a personal name used to identify a person in the Hebrew Old Testament. It is not presented here as a word describing an action, quality, or object, so its meaning is best understood as the person’s name rather than as a translated description. It occurs twice in the Hebrew corpus, at Genesis 25:13 and 1 Chronicles 1:29, and is rendered “Adbeel” in both passages. Its precise significance in either verse depends on the surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H1140.explanation: Binyah means a structure or building.

word:hebrew:H1243.explanation: Baqqarah means looking after. It can also mean seeking out, as a shepherd seeks out a scattered flock.

word:hebrew:H1306.explanation: Birsha is a personal name, rendered “Birsha.” It identifies one individual in the Hebrew Old Testament and does not function as a common word describing an action, quality, or object. The name occurs once, in Genesis 14:2. Because no short definition or broader lexical sense is available here, its secure meaning for a reader is its naming function: it identifies Birsha as a person. The surrounding verse determines his role in that passage, but the name itself primarily serves as a personal designation.

word:hebrew:H1359.explanation: Gôb is a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H1445.explanation: Geder is the name of a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H1517.explanation: Gîyd means a sinew or tendon.

word:hebrew:H1562.explanation: Gilalai is a personal name used to identify an individual in Nehemiah 12:36. It is not presented with an explicit definition describing an action, quality, or object; its function is naming rather than describing. This Hebrew word occurs once in the Hebrew corpus, so its supported meaning is limited to the name itself. The precise role of the named individual depends on the surrounding verse and passage.

word:hebrew:H1588.explanation: Gan means a garden, especially one enclosed or fenced.

word:hebrew:H1621.explanation: Gargᵉrôwth means the throat or neck.

word:hebrew:H1683.explanation: Deborah is a personal name. The name identifies Rebekah’s nurse and another Deborah, a prophetess who judged Israel.

word:hebrew:H1724.explanation: Daham means to be dumbfounded or astonished.

word:hebrew:H1799.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “records,” functioning as a noun for information preserved for later consultation. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs three times, all in Ezra, across two verses. Its use points to recorded material that can be consulted when documenting or checking matters. The exact force in either Ezra passage depends on the surrounding verse text, which is not included here.

word:hebrew:H1939.explanation: Hodaiah is a Hebrew personal name used to identify an individual, rather than a word describing an action, quality, or object. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, in 1 Chronicles 3:24, within a genealogical list. Because the available rendering presents it as a name and no lexical definition is supplied, its ordinary meaning here is its identifying function: it names a person. The surrounding verse text would be needed to say anything further about that individual or the name’s contextual significance.

word:hebrew:H1966.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “Lucifer,” the English rendering used for it. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Isaiah 14:12. Thus, its scriptural use is limited to that single occurrence rather than being a broadly repeated biblical term. The word functions as a distinctive designation in that passage; understanding its full force requires the surrounding verse and passage, which are not included here. Its identity is preserved as a Hebrew word and should not be merged with similarly rendered words from another biblical language.

word:hebrew:H1984.explanation: Hâlal means to praise or commend someone. It can also describe making someone foolish.

word:hebrew:H2026.explanation: Harag means to strike with deadly intent—to kill or slay.

word:hebrew:H2079.explanation: Zabbay is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H2112.explanation: Zûwaʻ means to shake with fear or tremble.

word:hebrew:H2167.explanation: Zamar means to make music with the voice or an instrument, including singing praises.

word:hebrew:H2268.explanation: Cheber is a personal name, rendered Heber in English.

word:hebrew:H2282.explanation: Chag means a festival or feast.

word:hebrew:H2365.explanation: Chushai is a personal name for an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H239.explanation: This Hebrew word expresses the meaning “good.” It functions as the sentence’s predicate, stating something about the people or subject being described. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, in Ecclesiastes 12:9. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding wording, since the available lexical information is limited. The word is therefore best understood at its basic level as a term describing goodness or favorable quality, without extending it into a more specific idea not established here.

word:hebrew:H2413.explanation: Chatam means to stop or refrain.

word:hebrew:H2538.explanation: Hamul is a personal name, rendered “Hamul.” It identifies an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or general object. This Hebrew name occurs three times in the Old Testament corpus: in Genesis 46:12, Numbers 26:21, and 1 Chronicles 2:5. Its precise significance as a name is not established by the available lexical information, so it is best understood simply as the proper name Hamul.

word:hebrew:H2620.explanation: Chasah means to flee for protection. It can also mean to confide in or put trust in.

word:hebrew:H266.explanation: Achochite refers to a descendant of Achoach. Scripture renders this designation “Ahohite.”

word:hebrew:H2695.explanation: This Hebrew word is a personal name, rendered “Hezro.” It identifies a man listed among David’s mighty men. The name appears three times in the Hebrew Old Testament, in two verses: twice in 2 Samuel 23:35 and once in 1 Chronicles 11:37. Because it functions as a name rather than a common noun or verb, its ordinary meaning is identification of this person, not a description of an action or quality.

word:hebrew:H2754.explanation: This Hebrew noun refers to “bags,” naming a physical object rather than an action or quality. It appears twice in the Old Testament corpus: once in 2 Kings 5:23 and once in Isaiah 3:22. In its recorded uses, the word functions as an object connected with handling or carrying. Its precise significance in either verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its ordinary lexical sense is straightforward: bags. The same meaning is represented in both available renderings.

word:hebrew:H2800.explanation: Harosheth is the name of a specific place. It functions as a proper name rather than a general description or action. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs three times, all in Judges 4, where the English rendering preserves the name as “Harosheth.” The word itself does not provide a broader meaning in the available passages, so its ordinary lexical sense is simply this geographical name. Its precise significance in any one occurrence depends on the surrounding verse and passage.

word:hebrew:H284.explanation: Ahihud is a personal name, rendered “Ahihud.” It does not have an explicit definition in the available lexical material, so it is best understood as the name of an individual rather than as a description or action. The name occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at 1 Chronicles 8:7. Its occurrence is associated with a genealogy and with a birth or begetting relationship, identifying it within a family record. The surrounding verse text would be needed to explain the individual’s specific role there.

word:hebrew:H2909.explanation: This Hebrew word means “shot.” It functions as an action word describing the act of shooting, rather than naming a person, object, or place. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Genesis 21:16. The surrounding verse determines the exact subject and circumstances of the shooting, but the word itself points plainly to that action. Its recorded use is connected with relationships involving a voice and a bow, reinforcing the sense of an action carried out by shooting.

word:hebrew:H2956.explanation: Tarad means to drive on continually.

word:hebrew:H3061.explanation: Yehud names Judah and can also name Judea.

word:hebrew:H3164.explanation: Jachdiel is the name of an Israelite, rendered Jahdiel in English.

word:hebrew:H3186.explanation: Yâchar means to delay or tarry longer.

word:hebrew:H3205.explanation: Yalad means to bear young or to beget. It can also describe the work of a midwife.

word:hebrew:H3348.explanation: Yaqeh is a name rendered Jakeh. Scripture identifies Jakeh as Agur’s father.

word:hebrew:H3429.explanation: Yôshêb bash-Shebeth is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H3476.explanation: Yosher means what is right or uprightness.

word:hebrew:H3494.explanation: Jethlah is a Hebrew proper name, preserved as “Jethlah” in the King James Version rather than translated as an ordinary descriptive word. It appears only once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Joshua 19:42. Because the available passage information does not include the verse text or surrounding context, this entry supports the name itself but does not establish whether it refers to a person, place, or something else. Its precise role depends on the wording of that passage.

word:hebrew:H3555.explanation: This Hebrew word means “burning.” It identifies burning as the subject being described, rather than expressing an action or command by itself. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs twice, both times in Exodus 21:25, so its recorded use is concentrated in a single passage. The surrounding verse determines the precise force of the term there, but its basic sense remains burning. This meaning is supported by the word’s English rendering and its occurrence record.

word:hebrew:H363.explanation: Ilan means a tree. A tree may grow strong and tall, with branches, leaves, and fruit.

word:hebrew:H3670.explanation: This Hebrew verb means “removed.” It functions as a verb, stating that its subject is described as removed rather than naming a person, object, or place. In the Hebrew Old Testament represented here, it occurs once, in Isaiah 30:20. That single occurrence establishes its basic lexical sense, while the exact force of the word within that specific sentence depends on the surrounding Hebrew sentence and its subject.

word:hebrew:H3753.explanation: This Hebrew word means “swift,” describing something that moves with speed or happens quickly. It serves as a descriptive word, drawing attention to rapid movement or action rather than naming a person or object. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Isaiah 66:20. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding context, but its basic sense remains speed, quickness, or swift movement.

word:hebrew:H3890.explanation: Levath is a preposition rendered “thee” (“you”) here.

word:hebrew:H3928.explanation: Limmud means taught, instructed, or learned. It can also describe someone accustomed to a way, including being accustomed to doing evil.

word:hebrew:H4055.explanation: Mad means a garment or other clothing.

word:hebrew:H4176.explanation: Moreh functions as a proper place-name in the Hebrew Old Testament. It identifies a location rather than expressing an action, quality, or relationship. The word appears three times, in Genesis, Deuteronomy, and Judges, and is consistently rendered “Moreh.” Because no verse text or surrounding context is included here, the specific significance of the place in each passage must be determined from its context.

word:hebrew:H4194.explanation: Maveth means death. It can also describe dying, and one passage renders it as “died.”

word:hebrew:H4253.explanation: Machlaphah means a lock or ringlet of hair.

word:hebrew:H433.explanation: Eloah means a deity or the Deity. In one passage, it refers to God as the one who made Jeshurun.

word:hebrew:H4370.explanation: This Hebrew noun means “breeches,” referring to a garment worn on the lower body. It appears five times in the Hebrew Old Testament, in passages concerning priestly clothing and related instructions. The word therefore identifies a specific item of clothing rather than an action, quality, or person. Its occurrences extend from Exodus through Ezekiel, showing its use in descriptions of sacred service and priestly dress.

word:hebrew:H4464.explanation: Mamzer means a bastard—specifically, a person born of a Jewish father and a heathen mother.

word:hebrew:H4705.explanation: Mits'ar means little or small in size or number. It can also refer to a short time.

word:hebrew:H4802.explanation: This Hebrew noun means “fryingpan,” naming a cooking utensil. It appears twice in the Old Testament, both times in Leviticus: in Leviticus 2:7 and Leviticus 7:9. The word identifies the pan used in preparing the food mentioned in those passages, distinguishing the utensil from the offering or food itself. Its basic function is therefore concrete and practical: it names an object used for cooking. The surrounding passage supplies the details of how that utensil is involved in each offering instruction.

word:hebrew:H4877.explanation: Meshobab is a Hebrew personal name, rendered “Meshobab.” It identifies an individual in the Old Testament and does not provide enough information here to establish a broader ordinary meaning or describe an action, quality, or object. The name occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at 1 Chronicles 4:34. Its precise significance as a personal name cannot be determined from the available lexical information, so it is best understood simply as the individual’s name in that genealogy.

word:hebrew:H4950.explanation: “Deep” describes something characterized by great depth. In the Hebrew Old Testament, this word appears only once, in Ezekiel 34:18, so its normal lexical range cannot be traced through many passages. Its recorded meaning is “deep,” functioning as a descriptive term for depth in the setting where it occurs. The surrounding verse text is needed to explain its precise force there; the word itself points to depth.

word:hebrew:H5034.explanation: Nabel means to wilt, fade, or fall away. It can also describe doing foolishly or treating something with little regard.

word:hebrew:H5089.explanation: The Hebrew word means “wailing,” referring to an expressed cry of grief or distress. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Ezekiel 7:11. Since the verse text and surrounding passage are not included here, the word alone establishes the idea of wailing but does not explain the full force of its use in that verse. Its meaning is therefore clear at the word level, while the specific emphasis depends on the surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H5108.explanation: Nôwb means produce or fruit, literally or figuratively.

word:hebrew:H5197.explanation: Nâṭaph means to drip or drop gradually. It can also describe speaking prophetically.

word:hebrew:H5203.explanation: Nātash means to leave or forsake. It can also mean to spread out.

word:hebrew:H5319.explanation: The word means “wrestlings,” a noun describing an act or state of wrestling. It names the experience or reality of wrestling rather than functioning as an action word. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, in Genesis 30:8, so its normal scriptural use is represented by this single occurrence. The word appears within a speech setting, helping identify it as language used to describe wrestling in the passage, while the surrounding verse is needed to explain its specific force there.

word:hebrew:H5346.explanation: Nekeb is a Hebrew place name, rendered as “Nekeb,” rather than an ordinary word describing an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, it occurs only once, in Joshua 19:33. Because it is a single geographic name and no explicit definition is preserved here, its meaning is best understood as the identity of the place called Nekeb, not as a broader theological or descriptive term.

word:hebrew:H5416.explanation: Nathan is a personal name. Nathan is called a prophet.

word:hebrew:H5449.explanation: Sabbal means a porter. It describes one who bears burdens.

word:hebrew:H558.explanation: Amatsjah is a personal name, rendered Amaziah in English.

word:hebrew:H5607.explanation: Çephēq means chastisement. It can also refer to sufficiency.

word:hebrew:H5672.explanation: Abiy means density, including depth or width, and can describe something thick.

word:hebrew:H5698.explanation: “Eglah” is a personal name, functioning as a proper noun rather than describing an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, this word appears twice, and both occurrences render the name “Eglah.” It is found in 2 Samuel 3:5 and 1 Chronicles 3:3. Without the surrounding verse text, the word itself identifies the person by name, while the passage supplies the details about her role or circumstances.

word:hebrew:H5751.explanation: ʻÔwd means while, marking the time when another event is taking place.

word:hebrew:H5878.explanation: Harod is a place-name, used to identify a specific location rather than describe an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, this word appears twice, both within Judges 7:1, so its use is highly concentrated. The English rendering preserves it as “Harod.” Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the word itself functions as a geographic name.

word:hebrew:H5892.explanation: ʻÎyr means a city or town.

word:hebrew:H5971.explanation: Am means a people, a gathered community. It can identify Israel as a distinct people and can also refer to multiple peoples.

word:hebrew:H6066.explanation: Onesh means a fine or imposed payment. It can also refer to punishment.

word:hebrew:H6084.explanation: Ophrah is a personal name and a place name.

word:hebrew:H6163.explanation: Arabiy means an Arabian or an inhabitant of Arabia. It can identify a person as Arabian, as with Geshem.

word:hebrew:H6237.explanation: Asar means to tithe—to take or give a tenth.

word:hebrew:H6310.explanation: Peh means mouth, literally or figuratively in speech. It can also refer to an edge or end.

word:hebrew:H635.explanation: Ester is a personal name rendered Esther, referring to the Jewish heroine.

word:hebrew:H6435.explanation: Pen means lest, warning of a possible unwanted result.

word:hebrew:H6480.explanation: Patsam means to rend or break, especially by an earthquake.

word:hebrew:H6501.explanation: Pereʾ means the onager, a wild donkey.

word:hebrew:H6633.explanation: Tsaba means to assemble or muster an army or servants.

word:hebrew:H6691.explanation: Tsophar is the name of one of Job’s friends.

word:hebrew:H6758.explanation: This word means “Zalmonah,” functioning as a proper name rather than an ordinary descriptive term. It occurs twice in the Old Testament Hebrew corpus, in Numbers 33:41 and 33:42, and the same English form is used in both places. Its primary function is to identify a named entity. The precise role of that name in either verse depends on the surrounding passage, since no short definition or verse text is available here.

word:hebrew:H680.explanation: Atsal can mean to reserve something.

word:hebrew:H6974.explanation: Qûwts means to awake or awaken from sleep. It can also describe Yahweh rousing himself to act against the nations.

word:hebrew:H6996.explanation: Qatan means small or little. It can describe something lesser in size, as with the lesser light. It can also refer to the youngest by age, or to someone who is little in his own estimation.

word:hebrew:H701.explanation: The word means “Arbite,” an identifying designation for a person. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, at 2 Samuel 23:35, and the available English renderings preserve it as “Arbite.” Because the verse text and surrounding context are not included here, the term can be recognized as a personal designation, while the passage itself supplies any further detail about whom it identifies.

word:hebrew:H7050.explanation: Qela primarily means a sling. It can also refer to a hanging screen, as in the hangings for the court.

word:hebrew:H7102.explanation: Qetsiah means cassia, a fragrant bark.

word:hebrew:H7177.explanation: Kartah is a Hebrew proper name, rendered as “Kartah.” It functions as a name rather than as an ordinary word describing an action, quality, or relationship. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, at Joshua 21:34. Because no explanatory definition or surrounding verse text is available here, the name itself is the clearest meaning available; its precise significance depends on the passage in which it appears.

word:hebrew:H7223.explanation: Rishon means first, marking what comes earliest in time or sequence. It can also describe a former or earlier time, referring back to something prior.

word:hebrew:H7281.explanation: Rega means a very short space of time, like a moment or instant.

word:hebrew:H7425.explanation: Remaliah is a personal name, rendered “Remaliah” in English. It identifies an individual in the Old Testament rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. The name occurs 13 times in the Hebrew Bible, especially in 2 Kings and Isaiah, and appears in passages connected with people, royal events, and spoken messages. Its precise significance in any particular verse comes from the surrounding passage, but its normal function is simply to name this person.

word:hebrew:H7490.explanation: Rea means to break or bruise.

word:hebrew:H7528.explanation: Ratsaph means to pave or tessellate a surface, like covering it with bright stones.

word:hebrew:H7627.explanation: Shebat is the name of a Jewish month.

word:hebrew:H7652.explanation: Sheba is the name of a place and is also used as a personal name.

word:hebrew:H7793.explanation: Shur is the name of a region of the desert.

word:hebrew:H7829.explanation: The Hebrew word means “consumption,” referring to something that consumes or wastes away. It appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, once in Leviticus 26:16 and once in Deuteronomy 28:22. In both places, it names a condition or consequence described as consumption. The word’s precise force in either verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central idea is a consuming, wasting effect rather than an ordinary act of eating.

word:hebrew:H7876.explanation: Shayah means to keep in memory; here it carries the sense of being unmindful.

word:hebrew:H7894.explanation: Shisha is a personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing a general idea or action. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at 1 Kings 4:3, and is rendered “Shisha.” Because this word functions as a name, its meaning is primarily its identification of that person, not a description of character, conduct, or an abstract concept. The surrounding verse supplies the information needed to understand Shisha’s particular role there.

word:hebrew:H7955.explanation: Shalah means a wrong or something amiss.

word:hebrew:H8020.explanation: Shalman is the name of a king apparently of Assyria; he destroyed Betharbel in battle.

word:hebrew:H806.explanation: Ashhur is the name of an Israelite, rendered Ashur in the English text.

word:hebrew:H8095.explanation: This Hebrew word is the proper name “Simeon.” It identifies Simeon as a person and, in later passages, the tribal family associated with him. The name appears 44 times in the Hebrew Old Testament, especially in genealogical lists and accounts of Israel’s tribes. Its use begins with Simeon’s birth and continues in references to his descendants and tribal identity. It functions as a name rather than a general description or action.

word:hebrew:H8154.explanation: Shasah means to plunder, rob, or spoil.

word:hebrew:H8213.explanation: Shaphel means to depress or sink, especially to bring something low. It can also describe humbling the proud.

word:hebrew:H8338.explanation: Shasha means to annihilate. In one usage, it is rendered “leave,” with only a sixth remaining.

word:hebrew:H8468.explanation: Tehinnah refers to a person named Tehinnah in a Hebrew genealogy. It functions as a personal name rather than as a common description or action. The word appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, in 1 Chronicles 4:12, within a record of family descent. Because no broader usage is recorded, its meaning is best understood as identifying this individual in that genealogy, rather than expressing a general idea used throughout Scripture.

word:hebrew:H8482.explanation: Tachtîy means lowermost or lower, describing something beneath another level.

word:hebrew:H8565.explanation: Tan means a monster or huge sea creature. It is rendered “whale” for a creature in the seas.

word:hebrew:H859.explanation: Attah means “you.” English translations may render it as “thou,” “thee,” “ye,” or “you,” depending on the translation.

word:hebrew:H8626.explanation: Taqan means to make straight or set in order.

word:hebrew:H943.explanation: Bûwk means to involve or entangle. It can also describe being perplexed.
